John — thanks, high level answers below and I've attached a short pack (DPA summary + SOC2 AOC + backup matrix). I'm happy to walk through live if you'd like.

Quick playbook (standard offering):
- Logical delete (T+0): When Medisys calls delete for an account or dataset we mark the object as deleted in the primary store immediately. This stops serving and removes indexing.
- Soft retention window (T+0 to T+30 days): Logical delete remains in metadata for 30 days to allow fast recovery / human error restoration.
- Background sanitization pass (T+30 to T+90): An automated scrub job iterates over deleted keys to overwrite/zero sensitive fields where supported by the datastore and clears any derived caches.
- Backup snapshot purge (T+180): Backups and point-in-time snapshots that include the deleted data are scheduled for purge at day 180 by default. Purge is manifest-driven: backups are tracked in a manifest and purged once no active legal hold references exist.
- Final cryptographic tombstone (proof-of-deletion): After purge we publish a deletion manifest & timestamp and can provide a signed confirmation (hash of manifest + timestamp) for audit purposes.

Options for extended timelines (paid/enterprise):
- Extended log retention: Standard: 12 months aggregated logs; Extended: 24–36 months available via add-on (supports SIEM export or hosted long-term store).
- Snapshot escrow: We can retain encrypted snapshots beyond T+180 in an escrow bucket for up to 12 months for an additional fee; 6–12 month escrow windows are common for customers with audit requirements.

Subprocessors & transfers:
- We maintain an up-to-date subprocessor list and data-flow diagram (see attached link). Cross-border backups: default-hosted backups may transit regional object stores; for EU data we localize the replicas with SCCs in place.

Compliance proofs attached: redwood_dpa_summary_v2.pdf, soc2_aoc_2026.pdf, backup_purge_matrix.xlsx.

If you're looking for a 36-month logs + 6-month escrow scope we'd propose the "Extended Sanitize & Preserve" addendum. If you'd like, I can draft language for the DPA (sanitization SLA clause) and a quote for the add-on.

Evelyn — thanks for the quick overview. A few follow-ups from legal/security:

1) Proof-of-deletion: we need a workflow that includes (a) confirmation the backup manifest purge has executed, and (b) a verifiable artifact we can store with our records (signed timestamp + manifest hash is acceptable). Please confirm whether that can be automated and delivered via an API call or a one-off report.

2) Logs: Medisys requires 36 months for certain audit-grade events (security & access logs). If this is possible only via an add-on, please provide pricing and whether logs will remain searchable or only exportable.

3) Escrow: For highly regulated customers we normally ask for 6 months of escrow retention of encrypted snapshots for compliance audits. Can Redwood do 6 months without a prohibitively large uplift?

4) Subprocessors & DTA: Provide the current subprocessor list and confirm whether any backup vendor stores replicas outside the EU for EU-subject data. If yes, confirm legal basis (SCCs or equivalent).

5) Redaction vs deletion: For some data types we prefer redaction (e.g., token replacement in logs) in lieu of full deletion. Does Redwood support redaction in the pipeline for PII fields? If not, what options exist?

We'd like the sanitized SLA clause drafted and added to the DPA before we circulate to procurement. Can you also add a short paragraph to the DPA on the preservation/hold process for litigation?

Thanks — if possible please respond by tomorrow so we can keep the procurement timeline on track.

Regards,
Lisa Moreno
Sr. Counsel, Medisys Healthcare

Lisa / John — appreciate the detailed asks. Below is an action-oriented reply and an explicit set of options so procurement has concrete language. I've also attached a draft "Sanitization SLA" doc (sanitization_sla_draft.docx) and linked the subprocessor list.

Proof-of-deletion (automated):
- We provide an API endpoint (DELETE /v1/audit/deletions/{job_id}/manifest) that returns the purge manifest, SHA256 digest, and a server-signed timestamp. We can also produce a one-off signed PDF report for procurement/legal on request.

Logs retention options (searchability vs archive):
- Standard (no-cost): 12 months searchable in-platform; exportable S3-compatible archive for longer retention.
- Extended (paid): 24–36 months searchable via warm archive (retention index) — pricing depends on retention length + query SLA. We'll attach a pricing card in the quote.

Escrow snapshots / snapshot carveouts:
- 6-month escrow is supported as an add-on (we typically encrypt with a customer-managed KMS key). Costs scale with snapshot retention size; operationally we create an "escrow bucket" with strict ACLs and retention manifest.

Redaction vs deletion:
- Redaction: We support field-level redaction pipelines for structured fields (PII tokenization or masking) prior to indexing. For unstructured text we offer a configurable PII redaction pass that can run at ingest or as a retroactive job during the sanitization window.
- If you require redaction-only for a data class we can add that policy to the DPA and treat delete as a redaction workflow instead of an irreversible purge.

Preservation / legal hold:
- Legal hold suspends purge manifests for an account/record and extends all retention clocks; holds are issued via the console or API and stamped in the manifest. We maintain an audit trail for hold issuance/expiration and can include hold metadata in the deletion proof.

Subprocessors & transfers:
- Current subprocessor list: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/medisys/subprocessors-2026.csv (includes storage, CDN, analytics vendors).
- For EU-subject backups we offer localized replicas and SCCs; cross-border replication is optional and controlled by region settings in the contract.

Next steps / proposed contract language (for procurement):
1) Add a "Sanitization SLA" clause to the DPA: outlines logical-delete, T+30 scrub, T+180 backup purge (default) and optional 6/12 month escrow retention.
2) Add an option table (Standard vs Extended) for logs and escrow with fees.
3) Add API deliverable for proof-of-deletion and a DocuSign link for signature of the DPA + addendum.

Action items:
- Evelyn: Draft DPA clause + pricing card — deliverable: sanitization_sla_draft.docx (attached).
- Grace: Confirm KM S integration notes & customer-managed KMS flow.
- Dev: Confirm API contract for deletion manifest endpoint and schedule enablement for escrow buckets.

If that works I can produce final contract language (we'll put the 36-month logs + 6-month escrow into the Extended quote) and send to procurement. Otherwise tell me which points you want tightened.
